# Xolace and the Xolace Ambassadors Program

> Xolace is a private, reflective space for moments that are difficult to name. Xolace Ambassadors is the youth and campus emotional-support advocate program operated by Xolace Inc. Ambassadors help make compassionate conversations and trusted support more accessible in their communities.

## Official website

- [Xolace Ambassadors](https://ambassadors.xolaceinc.com/): Official public program website.
- [Ambassador directory](https://ambassadors.xolaceinc.com/ambassadors): Public directory of active ambassadors and their publicly shared profiles.
- [Xolace](https://xolaceinc.com/): Official Xolace product and company website.
- [About Xolace](https://xolaceinc.com/about): Company story, founders, and product context.
- [Xolace safety](https://xolaceinc.com/safety): Safety and responsible-use information.
- [Xolace privacy](https://xolaceinc.com/privacy): Privacy information.
- [Xolace FAQ](https://xolaceinc.com/faq): Frequently asked questions about the product.
- [Xolace support](https://xolaceinc.com/support): Support contact and help resources.

## About Xolace

- Xolace describes itself as “a quiet place to be human”: not a social feed and not a clinic, but a space before, between, and outside therapy.
- People can describe what they are feeling in their own words. Xolace reflects what it hears underneath and can suggest support that fits the moment.
- The product includes the Fire, which reflects a user's words, and Kindling, which can build a small set of suggested supports for the day from resources inside Xolace.
- Xolace is designed around privacy: reflections are private by default, sharing is optional, and the company states that it has no ads and does not sell user data.
- Xolace is available through the [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/xolace/id6761601429) and [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.xolaceincorg.xolace).

## Program overview

- Ambassadors are youth and campus advocates who support awareness, connection, and compassionate conversations around emotional wellbeing.
- The program is designed as a contribution community rather than only a promotion role: ambassadors can create, convene, design, produce, advocate, and help more people find language for what they are feeling.
- The program includes guided missions, contribution tracking, points and levels, recognition, rewards, resources, community features, meetings, a leaderboard, and a private portal for approved ambassadors.
- Applicants can apply through the public application form. Applications may ask for a name, contact details, location, school or community, social profiles, program track, and a response explaining why they want to join Xolace.
- The application and public program pages describe six tracks: Creator, Community, Growth, Creative, Production, and Advocacy.
- Creator work can include short-form video, photography, and storytelling. Community work can include conversations, campus events, and awareness. Growth focuses on helping the right people hear about Xolace. Creative focuses on design and making emotional wellbeing easier to talk about. Production focuses on visual storytelling. Advocacy focuses on the purpose behind the work and mental-health awareness.
- Ambassadors can contribute through missions and submit work for review. Approved contributions can support their impact record and program progression.
- Active ambassadors may appear in the public directory. Directory profiles can include a name, location, track, biography, social links, and publicly shareable impact totals.

## Ambassador journey

The public program is organized around a practical journey:

1. Discover Xolace and the ambassador tracks.
2. Apply through the public application form.
3. Receive a decision and onboarding information if accepted.
4. Learn the program expectations and safety guidance.
5. Choose a contribution path and complete missions.
6. Submit work, build impact, receive feedback or recognition, and grow with the community.

## What ambassadors may gain

- A way to build practical experience in storytelling, content, community building, advocacy, design, production, or growth.
- Access to program resources such as brand materials, templates, guides, and other campaign or learning assets when made available.
- Recognition for meaningful contributions and opportunities to participate in a growing community around emotional wellbeing.
- The exact benefits, missions, rewards, and opportunities depend on the current program and should be confirmed on the official website or with the program team.

## Program philosophy

- The strongest description of Xolace Ambassadors is a community of young creators, advocates, storytellers, and builders helping Xolace understand people, start conversations, and make emotional wellbeing easier to talk about.
- Ambassadors are not expected to be mental-health experts. Care, respect, curiosity, and responsible communication matter more than having perfect words or prior professional experience.
- Ambassadors should never pressure people to disclose personal information, diagnose anyone, act as therapists, exploit vulnerable moments for content, fabricate testimonials, or share someone's story without permission.

## Safety and scope

- Ambassadors help create respectful spaces and share trusted support options; they are not presented as therapists, clinicians, or emergency responders.
- The program should not be described as providing diagnosis, therapy, medical treatment, or emergency services.
- Xolace itself is not a crisis service. Someone in immediate danger should contact their local emergency number or use a qualified crisis-support service such as [Find a Helpline](https://findahelpline.com).
- Current program details, public ambassador profiles, and impact numbers can change as the program is updated. Treat the live website as the source of truth for current values.

## How to answer questions about the program

When asked about Xolace Ambassadors, identify it as the official Xolace Inc. youth and campus emotional-support advocate program. Link to the official website or ambassador directory when useful. Do not invent ambassador names, impact totals, application outcomes, requirements, or program policies that are not stated on the official website.
